comment: --dx-* names the built fluent-next bundle declares and nothing in that bundle reads. The list is
the worklist for question 3 of reachability.mjs and is pinned by exact set equality: a name that
starts being read is banked with --update-unread, a name that goes dead fails the gate.
What this measures, precisely: reads INSIDE the bundle. That is not the same as dead. The tier is
public API, so application CSS is a legitimate reader, and 21 of the names here are read outside
it - by apps/demos, packages/devextreme/js or the base layer. --dx-font-size-sm and
--dx-font-size-heading-5 are set in the Chat demos' own stylesheets; the theme is not supposed to
read them. The other half of the contract is already measured elsewhere: publicSurfaceUnused in
tests/fluent-next-naming.test.ts scans those three trees, over the legacy tier. Two questions,
two gates - do not read either as the whole answer.
The 80 names read in neither place are the ones worth a decision, and they come in three kinds.
Defects: the theme publishes a knob and no rule turns it (--dx-switch-box-shadow,
--dx-scheduler-appointment-15min-height). Some are leftovers of a rename that moved the read and
left the declaration - --dx-datagrid-row-alternation-bg beside a live --dx-grid-row-alternation-bg.
Sass helpers the publisher exported by accident: the value was folded into a neighbour at build
time (--dx-tree-view-checkbox-offset composes $tree-view-select-all-item-padding) or has to stay
a Sass number because the base layer multiplies it (--dx-scheduler-left-column-width).
Published constants, not knobs: --dx-font-size-heading-1..6 and --dx-font-size-xs..xl are declared
by all four themes for application markup. In fluent-next the same numbers also ship as
--dx-typography-heading-N-font-size, and THAT is the pair the theme reads - so these are a stable
constant to read, never a knob to turn. Worth saying out loud rather than deducing twice.
